days.title: Trebuchet?!
days.approach: Each line is scanned with replace-megaparsec's sepCap for digit (and, in part 2, spelled-number) matches; the first match comes from the forward line, the last from parsing the reversed line against reversed words.
days.critique: Parsing the reversed line against reversed number words handles overlapping spellings like 'twone' without lookahead. Running sepCap over the whole line only to take the head does extra work, but it is linear and harmless here. uhead is partial, so a line with no match crashes. Input is embedded at compile time via Template Haskell.
days.html: module Day1 (part1, part2) where import Replace.Megaparsec (sepCap) import Text.Megaparsec (MonadParsec (try), choice, (<|>)) import Text.Megaparsec.Char (digitChar, string) import Prelude hiding (choice, digit, many, optional, string, try, (<|>)) numbers :: [String] numbers = ["one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine"] digit :: MParser ℤ' digit = uread . pure <$> digitChar word :: (String -> String) -> MParser ℤ' word f = choice (try <$> [string (f n) $> i | (n, i) <- zip numbers [1 ..]]) parser :: MParser ℤ' -> MParser ℤ' -> String -> ℤ' parser p q line = let go pq = rights . parserM (sepCap pq) in 10 * uhead (go p line) + uhead (go q (reverse line)) solve :: MParser ℤ' -> MParser ℤ' -> ℤ' solve p q = $(input 1) & lines & fmap (parser p q . unpack) & sum part1 :: ℤ' part1 = solve digit digit part2 :: ℤ' part2 = solve (digit <|> word id) (digit <|> word reverse)

days.title: Cube Conundrum
days.approach: A parser-combinator grammar builds Game records holding lists of Color draws. Part 1 keeps games whose draws stay within fixed limits; part 2 flattens draws and multiplies per-colour maxima.
days.critique: The Color sum type and the explicit three-accumulator go loop for r/g/b keep both parts short, linear in input, and easy to follow. The 12/13/14 limits are hard-coded literals. Input is spliced at compile time via Template Haskell, and because (⊢) returns a plain value rather than an Either or Maybe, the caller cannot handle a parse failure.
days.html: module Day2 (part1, part2) where data Color = Red ℤ' | Blue ℤ' | Green ℤ' data Game = Game {index :: ℤ', cubes :: [[Color]]} games :: Parser [Game] games = game `sepBy1` eol <* eof where color = do n <- number <* string " " choice [Red n <$ string "red", Green n <$ string "green", Blue n <$ string "blue"] game = do i <- string "Game " *> number <* string ": " Game i <$> (color `sepBy1` string ", ") `sepBy1` string "; " possibleGame :: Game -> 𝔹 possibleGame = all (all possibleColor) . cubes where possibleColor (Red i) = i <= 12 possibleColor (Green i) = i <= 13 possibleColor (Blue i) = i <= 14 power :: [Color] -> ℤ' power colors = go colors 0 0 0 where go [] r g b = r * g * b go ((Red i) : cs) r g b = go cs (max i r) g b go ((Green i) : cs) r g b = go cs r (max i g) b go ((Blue i) : cs) r g b = go cs r g (max i b) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 2) ⊢ games & filter possibleGame & fmap index & sum part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(input 2) ⊢ games & fmap (power . mconcat . cubes) & sum

days.title: Gear Ratios
days.approach: Scans the grid row by row, accumulating each digit run's characters and neighbour coordinates, then nubs them; part 1 keeps numbers bordering any Mark, part 2 groups numbers by adjacent '*' cells.
days.critique: The hand-written scanner repeats the same flush logic at a non-digit cell and at the row end. Neighbour lists grow by repeated list appends and are deduplicated with quadratic nub, while out-of-bounds coordinates are handled by catMaybes over (||?). Part 2 builds a per-number Map, merges with unionWith (<>), and keeps gears with exactly two numbers; foldl1 is partial if the grid has no numbers.
days.html: module Day3 (part1, part2) where data Cell = None | Digit Char | Mark Char deriving (Eq, Ord, Show) instance GridCell Cell where charMap = mkBimap $ [(None, '.')] <> [(Digit i, i) | i <- ['0' .. '9']] <> [(Mark c, c) | c <- "!@#$%^&*()-=/+"] getNumbers :: Grid Cell -> [(ℤ', [Coord2])] getNumbers g = go 0 0 "" [] where (maxX, maxY) = maxXY g go x y currentNum currentCoords | y > maxY = [] | x > maxX = case (currentNum, currentCoords) of (s@(_ : _), cs@(_ : _)) -> (uread s, nub cs) : go 0 (y + 1) "" [] _ -> go 0 (y + 1) "" [] | otherwise = case g ||! (x, y) of Digit c -> go (x + 1) y (currentNum <> [c]) (currentCoords <> neighbors (x, y)) _ -> case (currentNum, currentCoords) of (s@(_ : _), cs@(_ : _)) -> (uread s, nub cs) : go (x + 1) y "" [] _ -> go (x + 1) y "" [] isMark :: Cell -> 𝔹 isMark (Mark _) = True isMark _ = False part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(grid input 3) & ( \g -> getNumbers g & filter (\(_, cs) -> any isMark $ catMaybes [g ||? c | c <- cs]) ) & fmap fst & (Σ ˙) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(grid input 3) & ( \g -> getNumbers g & fmap (\(n, cs) -> mkMap [(c, [n]) | c <- cs, let a = g ||? c, a == Just (Mark '*')]) ) & foldl1 (unionWith (<>)) & mapFilter ((== 2) . length) <&> ꛛ & (ⵉ . elems)

days.title: Scratchcards
days.approach: Parses each card into an id and two number lists split at `|`; part 1 sums `2 ^ size (as ∩ bs) `div` 2`, part 2 folds over cards, adding each card's count to the next n card ids in a Map.
days.critique: The `2 ^ n `div` 2` form gives 0 for n = 0 without a branch, and one `parser` serves both parts. Part 2 uses an outer `foldl'` over cards and an inner `foldl'` over `[i + 1 .. i + n]` applying `adjust (+ c)`, so copies propagate forward as counts without materialising cards. Part 1 calls `parseWith parser` while part 2 uses the `⊢` operator for the same step, an inconsistency.
days.html: module Day4 (part1, part2) where parser :: Parser [(ℤ', [ℤ'], [ℤ'])] parser = many1 (line <* eol) <* eof where gap = many $ string " " line = do i <- (string "Card" >> gap) *> number <* (string ":" >> gap) as <- many1 (number <* gap) <* (string "|" >> gap) bs <- number `sepBy1` gap return (i, as, bs) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 4) & parseWith parser & fmap (\(_, as, bs) -> 2 ^ size (as ∩ bs) `div` 2) & sum part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(input 4) ⊢ parser & ( \cards -> foldl' ( \m (i, as, bs) -> let n = size (as ∩ bs) c = fromMaybe 0 $ m |? i in foldl' (flip (adjust (+ c))) m [i + 1 .. i + n] ) (mkMap [(i, 1) | (i, _, _) <- cards]) cards ) & unMap & fmap snd & sum

days.title: If You Give A Seed A Fertilizer
days.approach: Each map line becomes a forward and inverse partial function, combined per section as first-match-or-identity. Part 1 folds seeds forward; part 2 takes each line's first number as a candidate and checks it against the seed ranges.
days.critique: A single lambda over the swapped (source, dest) pairs produces both directions, so neither is written twice. Part 2 tests only the per-line dest numbers, combining the sections' inverse functions with `Ɍ ($)`. Range lookups scan linearly, the seed check rebuilds `chunksOf 2 seeds` for every candidate, and `toTuple2` is partial.
days.html: module Day5 (part1, part2) where parser :: Parser ([ℤ], [ℤ], [(ℤ -> ℤ, ℤ -> ℤ)]) parser = do seeds <- string "seeds: " *> (number `sepBy1` string " ") <* (eol >> eol) (mappings, destinations) <- unzip <$> (mapping `sepBy1` eol) <* eof return (seeds, concat destinations, mappings) where rangeLine = do (dest, source) <- let n = (number <* char ' ') in (,) <$> n <*> n rangeSize <- number <* eol return ( toTuple2 $ [(source, dest), (dest, source)] <&> ( \(a, b) x -> if (x >= a) && (x < a + rangeSize) then Just $ b + (x - a) else Nothing ), dest ) mapping = do many1 (noneOf "\n") >> eol (fs, destinations) <- unzip <$> many1 rangeLine let forwardBackward = toTuple2 $ [fst, snd] <&> ( \f x -> case catMaybes (f <$> fs <*> pure x) of [] -> x (x' : _) -> x' ) return (forwardBackward, destinations) part1 :: ℤ part1 = $(input 5) ⊢ parser & (\(seeds, _, mappings) -> flip (foldl' (flip fst)) mappings <$> seeds) & minimum part2 :: ℤ part2 = $(input 5) ⊢ parser & ( \(seeds, destinations, mappings) -> let validSeed seed = λ (⋁ [(seed >= a) && (seed < a + b) | [a, b] <- chunksOf 2 seeds]) in [d | d <- destinations, validSeed $ Ɍ ($) d ˙ (snd <$> mappings)] ) & minimum

days.title: Wait For It
days.approach: Parses times and distances as Doubles, solves the quadratic x(t−x) > d in closed form, and counts integers strictly between the roots via ceiling/floor; part 2 concatenates digits and reparses.
days.critique: The quadratic formula makes each race O(1), so part 2 needs no search, and `ceiling − floor − 1` counts only integers strictly between the roots, so exact integer roots are excluded correctly. All arithmetic, including the square root, is done in Double rather than integers. `asOne` builds the part-2 race by going through `round`, `show` and `uread` on each column, which works but is indirect.
days.html: module Day6 (part1, part2) where asMany :: Parser [(Double, Double)] asMany = do let l s = (string (s <> ":") >> whitespace) *> (number `sepBy` whitespace) zip <$> (l "Time" <* eol) <*> (l "Distance" <* eof) asOne :: Parser (Double, Double) asOne = asMany <&> (unzip >>> both (fmap (round >>> show) >>> mconcat >>> uread)) ways :: (Double, Double) -> ℤ' ways (t, d) = let f pm = ((-t `pm` sqrt (t ** 2 - 4 * d)) / (-2)) in ceiling (f (+)) - floor (f (-)) - 1 part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 6) ⊢ asMany & fmap ways & (Π ˙) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(input 6) ⊢ asOne & ways

days.title: Camel Cards
days.approach: Cards and hand types are enums with derived Ord. A tuple compare of (hand type, cards) sorts hands. Part 2 wraps cards in a JCard newtype that ranks jokers lowest and maps each type and joker count to an upgraded type. The sorted list is zipped with ranks.
days.critique: Using Ord instances and newtypes means the sort does all the ranking work. The joker upgrade is a hand-written case table over count patterns, which is long and easy to get wrong where a rule like 'add jokers to the largest group' would be shorter. charToCard and the Pair/TwoPair case are partial, and the parser also computes the final sum.
days.html: module Day7 (part1, part2) where data Card = C2 | C3 | C4 | C5 | C6 | C7 | C8 | C9 | CT | CJ | CQ | CK | CA deriving (Eq, Ord, Bounded, Enum) charToCard :: Char -> Card charToCard '2' = C2 charToCard '3' = C3 charToCard '4' = C4 charToCard '5' = C5 charToCard '6' = C6 charToCard '7' = C7 charToCard '8' = C8 charToCard '9' = C9 charToCard 'T' = CT charToCard 'J' = CJ charToCard 'Q' = CQ charToCard 'K' = CK charToCard 'A' = CA newtype JCard = JCard Card deriving (Eq) instance Ord JCard where JCard CJ <= JCard CJ = True JCard CJ <= _ = True JCard _ <= JCard CJ = False JCard a <= JCard b = a <= b data Hand = High | Pair | TwoPair | Three | FullHouse | Four | Five deriving (Eq, Ord, Bounded, Enum) data HandBid = HandBid [Card] ℤ' deriving (Eq) instance Ord HandBid where h@(HandBid cs _) <= h'@(HandBid cs' _) = (getHand h, cs) <= (getHand h', cs') newtype JHand = JHand HandBid deriving (Eq) instance Ord JHand where h@(JHand (HandBid cs _)) <= h'@(JHand (HandBid cs' _)) = (getHand h, JCard <$> cs) <= (getHand h', JCard <$> cs') class HasHand a where getHand :: a -> Hand instance HasHand HandBid where getHand (HandBid cards _) | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 5 = Five | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 4 = Four | isJust (reverseCounts |? 3) && isJust (reverseCounts |? 2) = FullHouse | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 3 = Three | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 2 = case reverseCounts |! 2 of [_] -> Pair [_, _] -> TwoPair | otherwise = High where reverseCounts = swapMapCollect $ countMap cards instance HasHand JHand where getHand (JHand (HandBid cards _)) | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 5 = Five | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 4 = case nj of 4 -> Five 1 -> Five _ -> Four | isJust (reverseCounts |? 3) && isJust (reverseCounts |? 2) = case nj of 3 -> Five 2 -> Five _ -> FullHouse | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 3 = case nj of 3 -> Four 1 -> Four _ -> Three | isJust $ reverseCounts |? 2 = case reverseCounts |! 2 of [_] -> case nj of 2 -> Three 1 -> Three _ -> Pair [_, _] -> case nj of 2 -> Four 1 -> FullHouse _ -> TwoPair | otherwise = case nj of 1 -> Pair _ -> High where counts = countMap cards reverseCounts = swapMapCollect counts nj = fromMaybe 0 $ counts |? CJ class HasBid a where getBid :: a -> ℤ' instance HasBid HandBid where getBid (HandBid _ bid) = bid instance HasBid JHand where getBid (JHand rh) = getBid rh parser :: (Ord a, HasBid a) => (([Card], ℤ') -> a) -> Parser ℤ' parser h = do cardsBids <- many1 ((,) <$> (charToCard <$$> (count 5 (oneOf "23456789TJKQA") <* string " ")) <*> (number <* eol)) <* eof return . sum . fmap (\(r, b) -> r * getBid b) $ zip [1 ..] . sort $ h <$> cardsBids part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 7) ⊢ parser (uncurry HandBid) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(input 7) ⊢ parser (JHand . uncurry HandBid)

days.title: Haunted Wasteland
days.approach: Parses the instruction string and node map with parser combinators, then lazily walks the cyclic L/R list to emit every step count at which a goal predicate holds. Part 2 takes each 'A'-ending start's first hit and folds them with lcm.
days.critique: Having travel return a lazy infinite list of hit times keeps one walker for both parts, with uhead taking the first hit. Part 2 combines only each start's first hit via lcm and never inspects later hits from the same list. The non-exhaustive case on 'L'/'R' and the (!! 2) indexing are partial functions.
days.html: module Day8 (part1, part2) where parser :: Parser ([Char], Map String (String, String)) parser = let name = count 3 alphaNum in (,) <$> (many1 (oneOf "LR") <* eol <* eol) <*> ( mkMap <$> many1 ( (,) <$> (name <* string " = (") <*> ( (,) <$> (name <* string ", ") <*> (name <* string ")" <* eol) ) ) <* eof ) travel :: (String -> 𝔹) -> String -> String -> Map String (String, String) -> [ℤ'] travel p s lr' g = go (cycle lr') 0 s where go (d : lr) n c | p c = n : next | otherwise = next where next = case d of 'L' -> go lr (n + 1) (fst $ g |! c) 'R' -> go lr (n + 1) (snd $ g |! c) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 8) ⊢ parser & uncurry (travel (== "ZZZ") "AAA") & uhead part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(input 8) ⊢ parser & ( \(lr, g) -> [ travel ((!! 2) >>> (== 'Z')) s lr g | s <- [s | (s, _) <- unMap g, s !! 2 == 'A'] ] ) <&> uhead & foldl1 lcm

days.title: Mirage Maintenance
days.approach: Each line is parsed into integers. A foldl' runs length−1 times, prepending successive difference rows, then foldr1 and the operator ((+) part 1, (-) part 2) combine each row's last or first element.
days.critique: Both parts share one solve, parameterised only by the element selector and the combining operator. It always builds all length−1 difference rows, so each line costs quadratic time and it never stops early when a row turns all zero. The whole pipeline in solve is a single point-free line of &&&, uncurry and flip, which makes the operand order of the final combination hard to follow.
days.html: module Day9 (part1, part2) where solve :: ([ℤ'] -> ℤ') -> (ℤ' -> ℤ' -> ℤ') -> String -> ℤ' solve get pm = parseWith (many1 ((number `sepBy` string " ") <* eol) <* eof) >>> fmap (pure &&& enumFromTo 2 . length >>> uncurry (foldl' (\(ds : dss) _ -> (uncurry (-) <$> zip (drop 1 ds) ds) : ds : dss)) >>> (fmap get >>> ((foldr1 pm . utail) &&& uhead) >>> uncurry (flip pm))) >>> sum part1 :: ℤ' part1 = solve ulast (+) $(input 9) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = solve uhead (-) $(input 9)

days.title: Pipe Maze
days.approach: Walks the loop from S in both directions, marking one side of each pipe as candidate outside cells. It BFS flood-fills non-loop regions, discards any region touching a marked cell, then drops whichever result contains (0,0).
days.critique: Marking a side of the loop during the walk replaces a separate shoelace or ray-casting pass, and the two walk directions cover both orientations. Choosing between the results by testing (0,0) assumes that cell is off the loop, so it sits in the exterior. The point-free part2 pipeline, built from both, &&& and uncurry, is hard to follow.
days.html: module Day10 (part1, part2) where data Cell = None | Start | PipeVertical | PipeHorizontal | PipeF | Pipe7 | PipeL | PipeJ deriving (Eq, Ord, Show) instance GridCell Cell where charMap = mkBimap [(None, '.'), (Start, 'S'), (PipeVertical, '|'), (PipeHorizontal, '-'), (PipeF, 'F'), (Pipe7, '7'), (PipeL, 'L'), (PipeJ, 'J')] pathOutside :: Grid Cell -> (([Coord2], Set Coord2), ([Coord2], Set Coord2)) pathOutside g = let pipesTo n@(x, y) c = c `elem` case g |? n of Just PipeVertical -> [(x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)] Just PipeHorizontal -> [(x + 1, y), (x - 1, y)] Just PipeF -> [(x + 1, y), (x, y + 1)] Just Pipe7 -> [(x - 1, y), (x, y + 1)] Just PipeL -> [(x + 1, y), (x, y - 1)] Just PipeJ -> [(x - 1, y), (x, y - 1)] _ -> [] outsideOf (x, y) (lx, ly) = case ((x - lx, y - ly), g |? (x, y)) of ((0, 1), Just PipeVertical) -> [(x + 1, y)] ((0, -1), Just PipeVertical) -> [(x - 1, y)] ((1, 0), Just PipeHorizontal) -> [(x, y - 1)] ((-1, 0), Just PipeHorizontal) -> [(x, y + 1)] ((0, -1), Just PipeF) -> [(x - 1, y), (x, y - 1)] ((-1, 0), Just PipeF) -> [(x + 1, y + 1)] ((1, 0), Just Pipe7) -> [(x + 1, y), (x, y - 1)] ((0, -1), Just Pipe7) -> [(x - 1, y + 1)] ((-1, 0), Just PipeL) -> [(x, y + 1), (x - 1, y)] ((0, 1), Just PipeL) -> [(x + 1, y - 1)] ((1, 0), Just PipeJ) -> [(x - 1, y - 1)] ((0, 1), Just PipeJ) -> [(x + 1, y), (x, y + 1)] _ -> [] start = gridFindOne Start g go path@(c : _) outside l reverse = let go' n = go (n : path) (foldl' (<-|) outside (outsideOf n c)) (Just c) reverse in case [n | n <- neighborsNoDiags c, Just n /= l, n `pipesTo` c, c == start || c `pipesTo` n] of [] -> (path, outside) (n : m : _) -> if reverse then go' m else go' n (n : _) -> go' n in both (go [start] ø Nothing) (False, True) enclosed :: Grid Cell -> Set Coord2 -> Set Coord2 -> Set Coord2 enclosed g path outside = let go seen Empty = (seen, seen) go seen (c :<| cs) | c ∈ (seen <> path) = go seen cs | c ∈ outside = (seen, ø) | otherwise = let ns = [n | n <- neighborsNoDiags c, n ∉ path, n ∈ g] in go (c |-> seen) (cs >< mkSeq ns) goAll _ es [] = es goAll seen es (start : starts) | start ∈ seen = goAll seen es starts | otherwise = let (seen', es') = go ø ([start] ⊐) in goAll (seen ∪ seen') (es ∪ es') starts in goAll ø ø [c | c <- coords g, c ∉ path] part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(grid input 10) & (pathOutside >>> fst . fst >>> length >>> (+ 1) >>> (`div` 2)) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(grid input 10) & ((enclosed >>> uncurry) &&& (pathOutside >>> both (first co))) & uncurry both & both (bool id (const ø) . (((0, 0) :: Coord2) ∈) &&& id >>> uncurry ($)) & uncurry (∪) & size

days.title: Cosmic Expansion
days.approach: Builds two sets of empty line indices, one per coordinate axis, then for every unordered galaxy pair walks each axis's coordinate range, counting 1 per index or the scale factor for empty ones.
days.critique: One function parameterised by the expansion factor serves both parts, and the inclusive `range` walk with a `- 2` correction handles endpoints uniformly. The empty-line sets are built inside the per-pair function `d`, so each pair rescans the grid unless GHC floats them out. The range walk is also linear in coordinate differences, where prefix sums over sorted coordinates would avoid that.
days.html: module Day11 (part1, part2) where distanceSum :: ℤ' -> Grid DotHash -> ℤ' distanceSum sc g = let es cons (a, b) = mkSet [i | i <- [0 .. a], all (== Dot) [g ||! cons i j | j <- [0 .. b]]] di (a, b) e = sum [bool 1 sc (i ∈ e) | i <- range a b] d ab = let m = maxXY g in di (fsts2 ab) (es (,) m) + di (snds2 ab) (es (flip (,)) (swap m)) - 2 in sum $ d <$> triPairs (gridFind Hash g) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(grid input 11) & distanceSum 2 part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(grid input 11) & distanceSum 1000000

days.title: Hot Springs
days.approach: Memoised recursion keyed on (remaining string, remaining group sizes): a leading '.' is prepended, each group is placed after a gap of i non-'#' cells, and recursive counts are summed. Part two unfolds records fivefold.
days.critique: Prepending '.' makes every placement a uniform gap-then-block step, keeping the recursion to two clauses. The memo key holds the whole string suffix, so key comparisons cost more as strings grow. For each candidate i it builds a Set from the gap take i ss and another from the block take c (drop i ss), and it tries every i rather than stopping once the gap hits a '#'.
days.html: module Day12 (part1, part2) where line :: Parser (String, [ℤ']) line = (,) <$> (many1 (oneOf ".#?") <* string " ") <*> (number `sepBy` string ",") ways :: (String, [ℤ']) -> Memo (String, [ℤ']) ℤ' ℤ' ways (ss, []) = return (bool 0 1 (all (∈ (".?" :: String)) ss)) ways (ss, c : cs) = treverse sum [ memo ways (drop (c + i) ss, cs) | i <- [1 .. length ss - c], '#' ∉ mkSet (take i ss), '.' ∉ mkSet (take c (drop i ss)) ] solve :: ((String, [ℤ']) -> (String, [ℤ'])) -> ℤ' solve f = $(input 12) & parseLinesWith line & fmap (f >>> first ('.' :) >>> ways >>> startEvalMemo) & sum part1 :: ℤ' part1 = solve id part2 :: ℤ' part2 = solve (bimap (intercalate "?" . replicate 5) (mconcat . replicate 5))

days.title: Point of Incidence
days.approach: Each candidate vertical and horizontal mirror line is checked by comparing the cell blocks on either side. Part 2 toggles every cell, recomputes reflections, and keeps lines absent from the original grid.
days.critique: Both axes are handled in one comprehension tagged Left/Right, so no code is duplicated, and partitionEithers keeps the final sum short. Part 2 is brute force, rerunning the full reflection scan once per toggled cell instead of finding lines with exactly one mismatch. The dense operators and the index arithmetic in `b` make the mirrored ranges hard to verify.
days.html: module Day13 (part1, part2) where reflects :: IntMapGrid Char -> Identity (Set (Either ℤ' ℤ')) reflects g = do (maxX, maxY) <- maxXYM g let b m0 m1 i = let w = min i (m0 - i + 1) in (([i - w .. i - 1], [0 .. m1]), ([i + w - 1, i + w - 2 .. i], [0 .. m1])) ((⊏⊐) <$>) . (fst <$$>) $ filterM (snd >>> bothM (\(xr, yr) -> sequence [g <||!> (x, y) | x <- xr, y <- yr]) >>> fmap (uncurry (==))) [(f i, s (b m0 m1 i)) | (f, (m0, m1), s, ir) <- [(Left, (maxX, maxY), id, [1 .. maxX]), (Right, (maxY, maxX), both swap, [1 .. maxY])], i <- ir] reflectsSmudged :: IntMapGrid Char -> Identity (Set (Either ℤ' ℤ')) reflectsSmudged g = do let toggle c g = g <||~> (c, bool '.' '#' . (== '.')) rs' <- traverse (\c -> (toggle c g >>= reflects) <* toggle c g) =<< coordsM g (setFilter <$> ((∌) <$> reflects g)) <*> pure (Ս ˙ rs') solve :: (IntMapGrid Char -> Identity (Set (Either ℤ' ℤ'))) -> Identity [IntMapGrid Char] -> Identity ℤ' solve f = fmap (uncurry (+) . second (* 100) . both sum . partitionEithers . concatMap co) . (traverse f =<<) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = runIdentity $ solve reflects $(gridsM input 13) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = runIdentity $ solve reflectsSmudged $(gridsM input 13)

days.title: Parabolic Reflector Dish
days.approach: Tilts by repeating a single-cell roll pass (`step`) over a VectorGrid until it stops changing (`iterateFix`), then sums row-weighted loads; part 2 indexes the `iterate oneCycle` sequence at 1000000000 using `(...)`.
days.critique: One `step` serves all four directions via `move`, `opposite` and `iterCoords`, keeping both parts short. Each tilt runs whole-grid passes until a fixpoint and compares full grids with `Eq` after every pass, rather than sliding rocks in one sweep. Part 2 relies on `(...)` selecting the 1000000000th element; its `Ord` constraint suggests repeat detection, but the shortcut is not visible here.
days.html: module Day14 (part1, part2) where step :: Dir2 -> VectorGrid Char -> VectorGrid Char step d g = let f g c = let c' = move d (-1) c in bool g (g ||. (c, 'O') ||. (c', '.')) ((g ||! c, g ||? c') == ('.', Just 'O')) in foldl' f g (iterCoords (opposite d) g) load :: VectorGrid Char -> ℤ' load g = sum ((1 + snd (maxXY g) -) . snd <$> gridFind 'O' g) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = load $ iterateFix (step DirUp) $(grid input 14) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = let oneCycle g = foldl' (\g d -> iterateFix (step d) g) g [DirUp, DirLeft, DirDown, DirRight] in load $ iterate oneCycle $(grid input 14) ... 1000000000

days.title: Lens Library
days.approach: Part 1 sums the HASH of each comma-separated step. Part 2 parses steps and folds them into 256 boxes, each a Map from label to focal length plus a Seq for lens order.
days.critique: Keeping a label-to-focal Map beside a Seq of labels separates lookup from ordering: '=' on an existing label rewrites only the Map entry, so the Seq order is preserved without searching it. Encoding '-' as ('-', 0) via pure 0 keeps one tuple type. The bool-based branches, with argument order (false, true), are harder to read than guards.
days.html: module Day15 (part1, part2) where hash :: String -> ℤ' hash = foldl' (\n c -> (n + ord c) * 17 `mod` 256) 0 part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 15) ⊢ csv & fmap hash & sum part2 :: ℤ' part2 = let op = (,) <$> many1 alphaNum <*> ((,) <$> char '=' <*> number <|> (,) <$> char '-' <*> pure 0) run m o = m |~ (hash (fst o), runOp o) runOp (l, ('=', f)) (m, s) = bool (m |. (l, f), s |> l) (m |. (l, f), s) (l ∈ m) runOp (l, ('-', _)) b@(m, s) = bool b (m |/ l, s >/< l) (l ∈ m) power (i, (m, s)) = sum [(i + 1) * slot * (m |! l) | (slot, l) <- zip [1 ..] (unSeq s)] boxes = mkMap [(i, (mkMap [], mkSeq [])) | i <- [0 .. 255]] in $(input 15) ⊢ (op `sepBy` char ',') & (foldl' run boxes >>> unMap >>> fmap power >>> sum)

days.title: The Floor Will Be Lava
days.approach: Worklist traversal over (coordinate, direction) states, destructured with `Empty`/`:<|` and extended with `<⊕`, recording a visited set and mapping each tile character to outgoing directions; part 2 maximises over perimeter starts.
days.critique: The mirror and splitter rules fit in one case expression, with `bool` choosing the turn per incoming axis, and keying `seen` on (cell, direction) stops beams from looping forever. Part 2 runs `energized` from scratch for each direction paired with the perimeter cells `pFrom` gives for it, a straightforward brute force. The case has no fallback branch, so an unexpected character crashes at runtime.
days.html: module Day16 (part1, part2) where energized :: Grid Char -> (Coord2, Dir2) -> ℤ' energized g start = let go seen Empty = size (setMap fst seen) go seen ((c, d) :<| q) | c ∉ g || (c, d) ∈ seen = go seen q | otherwise = let ds = case g ||! c of '.' -> [d] '-' -> bool [d] [DirLeft, DirRight] (d ∈ [DirUp, DirDown]) '|' -> bool [d] [DirUp, DirDown] (d ∈ [DirLeft, DirRight]) '/' -> [d & bool turnCW turnCCW (d ∈ [DirLeft, DirRight])] '\\' -> [d & bool turnCW turnCCW (d ∈ [DirUp, DirDown])] in go ((c, d) |-> seen) (q <⊕ [(move d 1 c, d) | d <- ds]) in go ø ([start] ⊐) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = energized $(grid input 16) ((0, 0), DirRight) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = let g = $(grid input 16) in maximum [energized g (c, d) | d <- enumerate, c <- perimeter g `pFrom` d]

days.title: Clumsy Crucible
days.approach: A* search over states (cell, current run length, direction) using a min-priority queue and Manhattan-distance heuristic, with turn and continue rules passed in as predicates for each part.
days.critique: One search serves both parts through the turnP/noTurnP predicates, and the goal check reuses turnP to enforce part 2's minimum run. Cost is charged on the cell being left and corrected at the goal by adding the target and subtracting the origin, which works but is hard to follow. Duplicate states are pruned only when popped, so the queue grows, and `(q <!)` is partial if no path exists.
days.html: module Day17 (part1, part2) where minimizeHeatLoss :: (ℤ' -> 𝔹) -> (ℤ' -> 𝔹) -> Grid ℤ' -> ℤ' minimizeHeatLoss turnP noTurnP g = let target = maxXY g go cache q | c == target && turnP l = cost + (g |! c) - (g |! (0, 0)) | k ∈ cache && cache |! k <= cost = go cache rest | otherwise = go cache' (foldl' (|.) rest next) where ((_, (cost, k@(c, l, d))), rest) = (q <!) cache' = if k ∈ cache then cache |~ (k, min cost) else cache |. (k, cost) next = [ (cost + (g |! c') + manhattan c' target, (cost + g |! c, (c', l', d'))) | (d', p, l') <- (d, noTurnP l, l + 1) : ((,turnP l,1) <$> [turnCW d, turnCCW d]), let c' = move d' 1 c, p && c' ∈ g ] in go (mkMap []) (mkMinQ [(0, (0, ((0, 0), 0, d))) | d <- [DirDown, DirRight]]) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(grid input 17) & minimizeHeatLoss (const True) (< 3) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(grid input 17) & minimizeHeatLoss (>= 4) (< 10)

days.title: Lavaduct Lagoon
days.approach: Parses each line into two (direction, length) instructions, selects one per part, then walks the polygon accumulating a shoelace-style area term and perimeter, combining them via Pick's theorem.
days.critique: One parser and one fold serve both parts, and accumulating `x' * (y' - y)` plus `p div 2 + 1` handles the large part 2 coordinates in O(n) without a grid. The area term is used without `abs`, so the sign depends on traversal orientation, which the code does not check. The part 2 direction comes from indexing the hard-coded list `[DirRight, DirDown, DirLeft, DirUp]` with a parsed `number`, a partial `!!` lookup.
days.html: module Day18 (part1, part2) where solve :: (((Dir2, ℤ'), (Dir2, ℤ')) -> (Dir2, ℤ')) -> ℤ' solve f = $(input 18) ⊢ ( f <$$> ( many ( (,) <$> ((,) <$> (udlrToDir2 <$> anyChar <* spaces) <*> (number <* spaces)) <*> ( swap <$> ( string "(#" *> ( (,) <$> (uread . ("0x" <>) <$> count 5 hexDigit) <*> (([DirRight, DirDown, DirLeft, DirUp] !!) <$> number) ) <* (char ')' >> eol) ) ) ) <* eof ) ) & pick (0, 0) 0 0 pick :: (ℤ', ℤ') -> ℤ' -> ℤ' -> [(Dir2, ℤ')] -> ℤ' pick _ p a [] = a + (p `div` 2) + 1 pick (x, y) p a ((d, l) : rest) = let (x', y') = move d l (x, y) in pick (x', y') (p + l) (a + x' * (y' - y)) rest part1 :: ℤ' part1 = solve fst part2 :: ℤ' part2 = solve snd

days.title: Aplenty
days.approach: Each rule is parsed once into a pair of a predicate closure and a symbolic condition; part 1 runs parts through the closures, part 2 walks backward from "A" over rule-prefix paths, intersecting xmas ranges.
days.critique: Building both representations in one parser pass serves both parts, and the backward search uses a map of paths keyed by destination; negating earlier conditions with `invert` gives disjoint ranges without forward interval splitting. Part 1's `uhead` fails if no rule in a workflow matches, and `|!` lookups assume every target exists. The 1–4000 bounds and "in" start are hard-coded.
days.html: module Day19 (part1, part2) where parser :: Parser (Map String [(Map Char ℤ' -> Maybe String, Either (Char, Char, ℤ', String) String)], [Map Char ℤ']) parser = (,) <$> (mkMap <$> (many1 (function <* eol) <* eol)) <*> (many1 (part <* eol) <* eof) function :: Parser (String, [(Map Char ℤ' -> Maybe String, Either (Char, Char, ℤ', String) String)]) function = let terminator = ((const . Just) &&& Right) <$> many1 alphaNum conditional = do k <- oneOf "xmas" opC <- oneOf "><" let op = mkMap [('>', (>)), ('<', (<))] |! opC bound <- number <* char ':' next <- many1 alphaNum return (\p -> if p |! k `op` bound then Just next else Nothing, Left (k, opC, bound, next)) in (,) <$> (many1 alphaNum <* char '{') <*> (((try conditional <|> try terminator) `sepBy1` char ',') <* char '}') part :: Parser (Map Char ℤ') part = char '{' *> (mkMap <$> ((,) <$> (anyChar <* char '=') <*> number) `sepBy1` char ',') <* char '}' apply :: Map String [Map Char ℤ' -> Maybe String] -> [Map Char ℤ'] -> ℤ' apply fs ps = let applyOne "A" p = sum $ snd <$> unMap p applyOne "R" _ = 0 applyOne f p = applyOne (uhead (catMaybes ((fs |! f) <*> pure p))) p in sum $ applyOne "in" <$> ps totalAccepted :: Map String [Either (Char, Char, ℤ', String) String] -> ℤ' totalAccepted fs = let target (Right s) = s target (Left (_, _, _, s)) = s paths = mkMapWith (<>) [ (target (ulast path), [(f, reverse path)]) | (f, conditionals) <- unMap fs, path <- inits conditionals, Λ ˙ (¬ null path), all isLeft (uinit path) ] invert (Left (c, '<', n, next)) = Left (c, '>', n - 1, next) invert (Left (c, '>', n, next)) = Left (c, '<', n + 1, next) invert c = c expand Nothing _ = 0 expand (Just xmas) [] = Π ˙ [b - a + 1 | (a, b) <- snd <$> unMap xmas] expand xmas ((Right _) : cs) = expand xmas cs expand (Just xmas) (Left (c, opC, bound, _) : cs) = let (a, b) = xmas |! c in case opC of '<' -> if bound <= a then 0 else expand (Just $ xmas |. (c, (a, min b (bound - 1)))) cs '>' -> if bound >= b then 0 else expand (Just $ xmas |. (c, (max a (bound + 1), b))) cs follow conditions "in" = expand (Just $ mkMap ((,(1, 4000)) <$> "xmas")) conditions follow conditions target = Σ ˙ [follow (conditions <> (p : (invert <$> ps))) f | (f, p : ps) <- paths |! target] in follow [] "A" part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 19) ⊢ parser & first (fst <$$>) & uncurry apply part2 :: ℤ' part2 = $(input 19) ⊢ parser & fst & (snd <$$>) & totalAccepted

days.title: Pulse Propagation
days.approach: Simulates pulses with a FIFO Seq queue per button press, timestamping each module's outputs; for each predecessor of hard-coded 'vf', takes the first output change's later press index plus 1, then multiplies.
days.critique: The per-module (press, signal) history makes part 2 a scan for the first output flip. Each processed pulse conses a full state map onto `ss`, never trimmed, and `stateChanges` reruns the 5000-press simulation once per predecessor. The 'vf' name and 5000 bound are input-specific, and `let Just (ts, fullName)` and `uhead` are partial.
days.html: module Day20 (part1, part2) where mkInitialState :: Map String [String] -> (ℤ', ℤ', [Map String (Map String 𝔹, [(ℤ', 𝔹)])], 𝔹) mkInitialState g = let gR = mkMapWith (<>) [(v, [k]) | (k, vs) <- unMap g, v <- vs] initialInputs "broadcaster" = mkMap [] initialInputs ('%' : _) = mkMap [] initialInputs ('&' : name) = mkMap [(inputName, False) | inputName <- gR |! name] s = mkMap [(name, (initialInputs name, [(0, False)])) | name <- keys g] in (0, 0, [s], False) pushButton :: ℤ' -> Map String [String] -> (ℤ', ℤ', [Map String (Map String 𝔹, [(ℤ', 𝔹)])], 𝔹) pushButton n' g = let go n st | n == n' = st | otherwise = go (n + 1) (onePass n g st) in let (low, high, ss, satisfied) = go 0 (mkInitialState g) in (n' + low, high, reverse ss, satisfied) onePass :: ℤ' -> Map String [String] -> (ℤ', ℤ', [Map String (Map String 𝔹, [(ℤ', 𝔹)])], 𝔹) -> (ℤ', ℤ', [Map String (Map String 𝔹, [(ℤ', 𝔹)])], 𝔹) onePass n g st = go st (mkSeq [("button", "broadcaster", False)]) where targets :: String -> Maybe ([String], String) targets name = case mapMaybe (\n -> (,n) <$> (g |? n)) ([id, ('%' :), ('&' :)] <*> pure name) of [] -> Nothing (ts, fullName) : _ -> Just (ts, fullName) go st Empty = st go (low, high, ss@(s : _), satisfied) ((origin, current, incomingSignal) :<| stack) = let Just (ts, fullName) = targets current (inputs, (_, signal) : _) = s |! fullName inputs' = inputs |. (origin, incomingSignal) signal' = case fullName of "broadcaster" -> Just False ('%' : _) -> if incomingSignal then Nothing else Just (ⴈ signal) ('&' : _) -> if all snd (unMap inputs') then Just False else Just True s' = s |~ (fullName, first (const inputs')) st' = let satisfied' = satisfied || ("rx" :: String) ∈ (ts :: [String]) && signal' == Just False in case signal' of Nothing -> (low, high, s' : ss, satisfied') Just False -> (low + length ts, high, (s' |~ (fullName, second ((n, False) :))) : ss, satisfied') Just True -> (low, high + length ts, (s' |~ (fullName, second ((n, True) :))) : ss, satisfied') in go st' $ case signal' of Nothing -> stack Just signalToSend -> stack >< mkSeq [(fullName, t, signalToSend) | t <- ts, isJust (targets t)] nameToHistory :: ℤ' -> Map String [String] -> String -> [(ℤ', 𝔹)] nameToHistory n g name = let (_, _, history, _) = pushButton n g in reverse $ ulast history `get` name where get h n = snd . uhead $ mapMaybe (h |?) ([id, ('%' :), ('&' :)] <*> pure n) stateChanges :: Map String [String] -> [[((ℤ', 𝔹), (ℤ', 𝔹))]] stateChanges g = ( \name -> let h = nameToHistory 5000 g name pairs = zip h (drop 1 h) in [p | p@((_, a), (_, b)) <- pairs, a /= b] ) <$> (let gR = mkMapWith (<>) [(v, [k]) | (k, vs) <- unMap g, v <- vs] in gR |! "vf") circuit :: Map String [String] circuit = $(input 20) ⊢ ( mkMap <$> ( many1 ( (,) <$> (many1 (oneOf "%&" <|> alphaNum) <* string " -> ") <*> (many1 alphaNum `sepBy1` string ", " <* eol) ) <* eof ) ) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = circuit & pushButton 1000 & (\(low, high, _, _) -> (low, high)) & uncurry (*) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = circuit & stateChanges & fmap ((snd >>> fst >>> (+ 1)) . uhead) & (Π ˙)

days.title: Step Counter
days.approach: Both parts expand a Set of reachable plots one step at a time. Part 2 tiles the grid via modular lookups, records set sizes when `n mod 131 == 65` (steps 65, 196, 327), and extrapolates quadratically.
days.critique: The frontier-set simulation is short, and a finite-difference quadratic fit avoids simulating 26501365 steps. The constants 131, 65 and 393 are hard-coded, and the extrapolation assumes the counts grow quadratically at those intervals, which the code does not check. Each step rebuilds a Set from all neighbours, `let [a, b, c]` is a partial pattern, and `do` wraps a pure value.
days.html: module Day21 (part1, part2) where walk :: ℤ' -> Grid Char -> ℤ' walk n g' = size (go n (mkSet [start])) where start = gridFindOne 'S' g' g = g' |. (start, '.') go 0 cs = cs go n cs = go (n - 1) (setFilter (\c -> g |? c == Just '.') . setConcatMap (co . neighborsNoDiags) $ cs) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = walk 64 $(grid input 21) part2 :: ℤ' part2 = do let g = $(grid input 21) :: Grid Char cs = mkSet (gridFind 'S' g) spaces = cs ∪ mkSet (gridFind '.' g) go n cs | n == 393 = [] | n `mod` 131 == 65 = size cs : next | otherwise = next where next = go (n + 1) ( mkSet [ (x, y) | c <- (cs ⊏⊐), (x, y) <- neighborsNoDiags c, (mod x 131, mod y 131) ∈ spaces ] ) poly n = let [a, b, c] = go 0 cs in a + n * (b - a + (n - 1) * (c + a - 2 * b) `div` 2) in poly (26501365 `div` 131)

days.title: Sand Slabs
days.approach: Bricks are sorted by z and settled by repeated passes that lower each unsupported brick one unit until a fixpoint. Pairwise support maps answer part 1 and drive an iterated fallen-set expansion for part 2.
days.critique: Two Map Brick (Set Brick) support relations make both parts short comprehensions, and endpoint order is normalised with min/max. Settling is slow: a pass moves each brick at most one unit with an O(n) any-check per brick. The maps need O(n²) pairwise tests, and part 2 re-filters the surviving set every round for each starting brick.
days.html: module Day22 (part1, part2) where type Brick = (Coord3, Coord3) overlapping :: (Ord a) => (a, a) -> (a, a) -> 𝔹 overlapping (a', b') (c', d') = let (a, b) = (min a' b', max a' b') (c, d) = (min c' d', max c' d') in a <= d && b >= c restingOn :: Brick -> Brick -> 𝔹 restingOn ((x, y, z), (x', y', z')) ((x'', y'', z''), (x''', y''', z''')) = min z z' == max z'' z''' + 1 && overlapping (x, x') (x'', x''') && overlapping (y, y') (y'', y''') onFloor :: Brick -> 𝔹 onFloor ((_, _, z), (_, _, z')) = min z z' == 1 freefall :: Vector Brick -> Vector Brick freefall bricks = let go bricks i = let brick = bricks !! i in if onFloor brick || (brick `restingOn`) `any` bricks then bricks else bricks !. (i, both (move3 D3zN 1) brick) fallOnce bricks' = foldl' go bricks' [0 .. length bricks' - 1] in iterateFix fallOnce bricks structure :: Vector Brick -> (Map Brick (Set Brick), Map Brick (Set Brick)) structure bricks = let m :: (Brick -> Brick -> 𝔹) -> Map Brick (Set Brick) m f = mkWith (∪) ( [ (brick, co [brick']) | brick <- bricks, brick' <- bricks, brick /= brick', brick `f` brick' ] ) in both m (restingOn, flip restingOn) disintegrateOne :: Vector Brick -> ℤ' disintegrateOne bricks = let (brickRestingOn, restingOnBrick) = structure bricks in size [ brick | brick <- bricks, brick ∉ restingOnBrick || all ((&&) <$> (∈ brickRestingOn) <*> ((brickRestingOn |!) >>> (/= co [brick]))) (restingOnBrick |! brick) ] disintegrateAll :: Vector Brick -> ℤ' disintegrateAll bricks = let brickRestingOn = fst $ structure bricks in sum [ subtract 1 . size . fst $ iterateFix ( \(fallen, bricks) -> let fallen' = setFilter (\brick -> (ȣ ¬ onFloor brick) && brickRestingOn |! brick ∖ fallen == ø) bricks in (fallen ∪ fallen', bricks ∖ fallen') ) (co ([brick], bricks)) | brick <- bricks ] fallen :: Vector Brick fallen = $(input 22) ⊢ (toTuple2 <$$> (toTuple3 <$$$> many1 (((number `sepBy1` char ',') `sepBy1` char '~') <* eol) <* eof)) & sortOn (thd3 . snd) & mkVec & freefall part1 :: ℤ' part1 = disintegrateOne fallen part2 :: ℤ' part2 = disintegrateAll fallen

days.title: A Long Walk
days.approach: Part 1 enumerates paths with a queue of (cell, visited-set) states, moving any direction on '.' but only arrow-wise on slopes. Part 2 builds a junction graph (convolution-found forks plus start/end) and runs exhaustive DFS.
days.critique: Junction compression keeps Part 2's exhaustive search tractable. mkGraph runs a full slopePaths search for every junction pair from triPairs, adjacent or not, repeating grid work. Part 1 keeps every complete path set in memory before taking the maximum length. maximum and |! are partial, and -1 stands in for no path.
days.html: module Day23 (part1, part2) where slopePaths :: (Char -> [Dir2]) -> (Coord2 -> 𝔹) -> Coord2 -> Coord2 -> Grid Char -> [Set Coord2] slopePaths ns stopping start end g = let go Empty paths = paths go ((c, s) :<| q) paths | c == end = go q (end |-> s : paths) | c /= start && stopping c || c ∈ s = go q paths | otherwise = let q' = mk [ (c', c |-> s) | c' <- move <$> ns (g |! c) <*> pure 1 <*> pure c, g |? c' ∈ (Just <$> (".<>^v" :: String)) ] in go (q >< q') paths in go (mkSeq [(start, ø)]) [] forks :: Grid Char -> Set Coord2 forks = co . gridFind True . convolve (1, 1, 1, 1) ( \g -> g |? (0, 0) == Just '.' && length ( filter (∈ (Just <$> (".<>^v" :: String))) ((g |?) <$> neighborsNoDiags (0, 0)) ) > 2 ) mkGraph :: Grid Char -> Set Coord2 -> Map Coord2 (Map Coord2 [Set Coord2]) mkGraph g forks = fmap (mkMapWith (<>)) . mkMapWith (<>) . mconcat $ [ [(start, [(end, [path])]), (end, [(start, [path])])] | (start, end) <- triPairs forks, path <- slopePaths (const enumerate) (∈ forks) start end g ] allPaths :: Map Coord2 (Map Coord2 [Set Coord2]) -> Coord2 -> Coord2 -> ℤ' allPaths graph start end = fromMaybe (-1) $ go start ø where go a seen | a == end = Just 0 | a ∈ seen = Nothing | otherwise = case catMaybes [ (-1 + size p +) <$> go b (a |-> seen) | (b, ps) <- unMap (graph |! a), b ∉ seen, p <- ps ] of [] -> Nothing ls -> Just (maximum ls) parts :: (ℤ', ℤ') parts = let g = $(grid input 23) (start, end) = ((1, 0), first (subtract 1) (maxXY g)) paths = slopePaths (\c -> bool [fromArrow2 c] enumerate (c == '.')) (const False) start end g graph = mkGraph g (co [start, end] ∪ forks g) in (subtract 1 . maximum . fmap length $ paths, allPaths graph start end) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = fst parts part2 :: ℤ' part2 = snd parts

days.title: Never Tell Me The Odds
days.approach: Part 1 intersects every hailstone pair's 2D slope-intercept lines over exact rationals, filtering by bounds and future time; part 2 gives Z3 position-plus-velocity equations for all stones.
days.critique: Exact rationals avoid floating-point error, and Z3 solves part 2 with little algebra. `t'` is computed from the first stone's `x` and `vx`, duplicating `t`; the second stone's future check really comes from its own `validIntersection` call, where `inFuture` uses its values. A zero x- or y-velocity can divide by zero. Part 2 adds a time variable per stone where three stones suffice.
days.html: module Day24 (part1, part2) where data Intersection = NoIntersection | IntersectAt (ℚ, ℚ) ℚ ℚ | Parallel ℚ ℚ intersect2d :: (ℚ, ℚ) -> (ℚ, ℚ) -> (ℚ, ℚ) -> (ℚ, ℚ) -> Intersection intersect2d (x, y) (vx, vy) (x', y') (vx', vy') | m == m' && c == c' = Parallel m c | m == m' = NoIntersection | t >= 0 && t' >= 0 = IntersectAt (ix, iy) t t' | otherwise = NoIntersection where m = vy / vx c = y - (m * x) m' = vy' / vx' c' = y' - (m' * x') ix = (c' - c) / (m - m') iy = m * ix + c t = (ix - x) / vx t' = (ix - x) / vx inFuture :: (ℚ, ℚ) -> (ℚ, ℚ) -> (ℚ, ℚ) -> 𝔹 inFuture (x, y) (vx, vy) (ix, iy) = (ix - x) / vx >= 0 && (iy - y) / vy >= 0 validIntersection :: (ℚ, ℚ) -> (ℚ, ℚ) -> (ℚ, ℚ) -> Intersection -> 𝔹 validIntersection _ _ _ NoIntersection = False validIntersection (low, high) (x, y) (vx, vy) (IntersectAt (ix, iy) t t') = ix >= low && iy >= low && ix <= high && iy <= high && inFuture (x, y) (vx, vy) (ix, iy) && t >= 0 && t' >= 0 validIntersection (low, high) (x, y) (vx, vy) (Parallel m c) = let f x = m * x + c g y = (y - c) / m in any (\(a, b) -> validIntersection (low, high) (x, y) (vx, vy) (intersect2d (x, y) (vx, vy) (a, b) (0, 0))) [(low, f low), (high, f high), (g low, low), (g high, high)] intersections :: (ℚ, ℚ) -> [((ℚ, ℚ, ℚ), (ℚ, ℚ, ℚ))] -> [Intersection] intersections lowHigh stones = [ i | (((x, y, _), (vx, vy, _)), ((x', y', _), (vx', vy', _))) <- triPairs stones, let i = intersect2d (x, y) (vx, vy) (x', y') (vx', vy'), validIntersection lowHigh (x, y) (vx, vy) i, validIntersection lowHigh (x', y') (vx', vy') i ] stones :: [((ℚ, ℚ, ℚ), (ℚ, ℚ, ℚ))] stones = $(input 24) ⊢ ( let c3 = toTuple3 <$> count 3 ((fromIntegral <$> number) <* optional (char ',' >> many (char ' '))) in many1 ((,) <$> (c3 <* (string " @" >> many (char ' '))) <*> c3 <* eol) <* eof ) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = stones & intersections (200000000000000 % 1, 400000000000000 % 1) & length part2 :: ℤ part2 = z3 do [x, y, z, vx, vy, vz] <- traverse mkFreshRealVar ["x", "y", "z", "vx", "vy", "vz"] forM_ (zip [0 ..] stones) ( \(i, stone) -> do t <- mkFreshRealVar ("t" <> show i) [x', y', z', vx', vy', vz'] <- traverse (mkRealNum . fromRational) (uncurry (<>) (both toList3 stone)) sequence [ do a <- mkAdd . (p :) . pure =<< mkMul [t, v] b <- mkAdd . (p' :) . pure =<< mkMul [t, v'] assert =<< mkEq a b | (p, v, p', v') <- [(x, vx, x', vx'), (y, vy, y', vy'), (z, vz, z', vz')] ] ) round . sum . concatMap catMaybes . snd <$> withModel (evalReal >>> forM [x, y, z])

days.title: Snowverload
days.approach: Parses lines into (node, neighbours) pairs, builds an adjacency map with mkMap and a reversed one with swapMapList, merges them via unionWith (<>), then counts nodes reachable while skipping three literal edges.
days.critique: The three cut edges are hard-coded node-name literals, so nothing computes the minimum cut and the solution depends on a specific input's edge names. The traversal is short: a queue matched with Empty and :<| plus a visited set, multiplying component size by the remainder. `count 3 alphaNum` assumes three-character names.
days.html: module Day25 (part1, part2) where traverseWithout :: [(String, String)] -> Map String [String] -> ℤ' traverseWithout abc g = go ø (take 1 (keys g) ⊐) where go seen Empty = size seen go seen (a :<| q) | a ∈ seen = go seen q | otherwise = go (a |-> seen) (q <⊕ [b | b <- fromMaybe [] $ g |? a, (a, b) ∉ abc, (b, a) ∉ abc]) part1 :: ℤ' part1 = $(input 25) ⊢ (let s = count 3 alphaNum in many1 ((,) <$> (s <* string ": ") <*> (s `sepBy` char ' ') <* eol) <* eof) & mkMap & (id &&& swapMapList) & uncurry (unionWith (<>)) & (traverseWithout [("vfx", "bgl"), ("bqq", "rxt"), ("btp", "qxr")] &&& size) & (\(a, b) -> a * (b - a)) part2 :: Text part2 = "Merry Christmas!"
